messages:
Anya: Quick sync — Q3/Q4 capacity alignment. APAC forecast just increased ~40% after the new partner pilot. Need options: accelerate H100 buys, re-route NA capacity, or tighten routing/cost controls. Decision end of day?

Maria: Can we get the exact uplift numbers? rough % is fine. need to see peak concurrency vs tokens. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Lee: From procurement side — lead time for H100 discrete racks is ~14-18 weeks if we start now. A100 stock is available in 6-8 weeks but 2x the rack count for same throughput. Tradeoff = cost + ops complexity.

Sam: Remind folks: capex commit windows for reserved nodes end of next month. If we want discounted reserved pricing for Dedicated pools we need to lock by 2026-06-10. :warning:

Jordan: Utilization targets we agreed for 2026 Q4 = 72% fleet average. If APAC spikes we either accept lower latency (spill to hosted NA), or push up autoscale thresholds and pay more for burst GPUs.

Priya: Customer ask: EU latency-sensitive tenant requires <80ms p95 and cannot be routed via NA for compliance. That reduces our flexibility to move EU -> NA. APAC partner is non-compliant for EU so no impact there.

Maria: Copy of quick forecast snippet I pulled from analytics — rough but actionable:
```
region,current_qtr,projected_q4,pct_growth
NA,120M tokens,140M tokens,16%
EU,80M tokens,96M tokens,20%
APAC,42M tokens,94M tokens,124%
peak_concurrency_est,NA:550,EU:320,APAC:480
```

Lee: Given that, two pragmatic paths:
1) Accelerate partial H100 buy for APAC cluster (enough for q4 projected peak + 15% buffer). Procure now, deploy to SG region. Pros: lower tail latency, consistent performance. Cons: capex and 4mo lead time.
2) Short-term: shift existing NA pooled capacity + enable aggressive autoscaling + tighter routing policies (force non-latency-critical workloads to cheaper quantized models). Pros: fast, low capex. Cons: higher p95 for APAC and complexity in routing rules.

Sam: Cost numbers rough estimate: H100 partial buy = +$1.2M capex for target cluster. Shifting NA capacity (software) = $0 capex, ops cost ~0.1 FTE/month and ~$80k/mo cloud egress/replication during peak.

Jordan: Operational risk note: moving stateful model caches cross-region will blow KV cache cold-starts for many sessions — expect 15-30% token cost spike for first 48h per workload. Need canary and warmup runbook.

Priya: Customers with SLAs: two enterprise accounts flagged — both in APAC, one requires private deployment option (Dedicated). If we don't accelerate hardware, we'll need to convert them to Dedicated (reserved), which is revenue but different margin profile.

Anya: Suggested decision framework:
- Safety: ensure EU SLAs never routed off-region.
- Near-term (Q3-Q4): prefer software mitigations + 15% burst plan unless we can secure <16 week H100 delivery.
- Long-term: aim for APAC permanent cluster H100 by end of Q4 if budget approved.

Lee: I'll reach out to procurement today to get updated lead times and firm quotes. If we can hit 12-14 weeks that's a green light for partial buy.

Maria: I'll model 3 scenarios in the deck: (A) Do nothing (SW only), (B) Hybrid (SW + limited H100), (C) Full H100 cluster. Will include customer SLA impacts and forecasted unit economics.

Sam: I'll calc lease vs buy and reserved contract windows and post numbers here by noon.

Jordan: I'll draft a warmup/canary plan for cross-region warm caches and a rollback checklist.

Priya: I'll coordinate with AE to surface enterprise willingness to convert to Dedicated. Might accelerate decision if revenue covers capex.

Anya: OK — owners listed. Can we reconvene at 16:00 PT for a quick alignment with Finance and Procurement? If anyone can't, DM me. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder: procurement ticket #PR-4887 created by Lee for H100 vendor quotes. https://re.dwood/proc/PR-4887

Lee: Ticket updated with initial quotes, expected lead time 14-16 weeks from signed PO. Putting estimate on calendar.

Anya: Great. Final ask before 16:00: drop any hard blockers in this thread. Otherwise we'll prioritize hybrid path and present options to Exec. :ok_hand:
